topics.description: Iceni queen who led a major revolt against Roman rule in Britain during the reign of Nero.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: During this ruler’s reign, the Iceni (ee-KAY-nee) tribe rose in revolt, led by Boudicca. This emperor forced his Stoic tutor, Seneca, to commit suicide before his family. This man’s mother, Agrippina, dominated his decisions until he had her killed off. This last emperor of the Julio-Claudian dynasty is said to have blamed Christians for the Great (*) Fire of Rome. For ten points, what emperor is said to have played the violin as Rome burned?
parts.answer: Nero [or Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A governor of this region brutally defeated Calgacus (kal-GAK-us) to the north of this region at  the Battle of Mons Graupius (MAHNZ GRAO-pee-us). Caligula's (kuh-LIG-yoo-luh's) aborted  invasion of this area ended with orders for his troops to gather (*) seashells. Claudius brought  elephants during the successful Roman conquest of this region. The Battle of Watling Street ended a  rebellion in this region during the reign of Nero that was led by the Iceni (ai-SEE-nee) queen Boudica  (BOO-dee-kah). For 10 points, name this region that Julius Caesar briefly invaded by crossing a channel  from Gaul.
parts.answer: Britain [or Roman Britain; or Britannia; or Great Britain; or England; do not accept or  prompt on “United Kingdom”]

topics.description: A Chinese-led global infrastructure and investment initiative that expands transportation, trade, connectivity, and economic ties among participating countries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country's JobKeeper program provided financial assistance during the COVID pandemic. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country that canceled the visa of tennis star Novak Djokovic (NO-vac JOE-kuh-vich) in January 2022 over a lack of COVID vaccination.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This politician overcame a COVID infection during campaigning and succeeded Scott Morrison as Australian prime minister in 2022.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Australia's government announced in 2022 the cancellation of the state of Victoria's participation in this worldwide Chinese project of infrastructure financing.
parts.answer: Belt and Road Initiative [or Dài yīlù]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This modern-day leader is protected online by the 50 Cent Army who spam critical posts. This leader’s administration outlined “Eight Musts” promoting his country’s “peaceful development” and “social harmony.” Terry Branstad was tapped as ambassador to this leader’s country due to his time spent in Muscatine, Iowa as an agricultural delegate. In 2021 textbooks on this leader’s namesake (*) “Thought” were added to his country’s school curriculum. The Belt and Road Initiative began under this leader, who banned satirical depictions of him as Winnie the Pooh. For 10 points, name this current president of China.
parts.answer: Xi Jinping [shee jeen-peeng] [accept Xi Jinping Thought or Xiism]

topics.description: The Islamic caliphate founded in 750 that ruled much of the Muslim world from Baghdad until the thirteenth century.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Palace of the Golden Gate was at the center of this city’s original “Round” design. This city’s Nahrawan Canal was destroyed by Turkish ghulams revolting with the Buyid dynasty. The Barmakid family financed the Translation Movement of Greek Texts in this city at an institution rumored to serve as a (*) library for Al-Mansur. The last ruler of a dynasty based in this city was wrapped in a carpet and trampled by the horses of Hulegu Khan. Harun al-Rashid established the House of Wisdom in this city. For 10 points, name this capital of the Abbasid Caliphate during the Islamic Golden Age that now serves as the capital of Iraq.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Tigris River apocryphally ran black with ink when this city’s House of Wisdom was sacked in 1258. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this medieval center of Islamic learning, the modern-day capital of Iraq

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Baghdad was once the capital of this Islamic caliphate, which came to power following Abu Muslim’s revolution against the Umayyad Caliphate.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Mills for producing this substance emerged in Baghdad after the methods were divulged by Chinese prisoners. This substance was among China’s Four Great Inventions.

topics.description: The 1485 battle in which Henry Tudor defeated Richard III, ending the Wars of the Roses and helping establish the Tudor dynasty.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One leader in this conflict adopted the symbol of the sun in splendor after seeing an atmospheric phenomenon called a sun dog at the Battle of Mortimer’s Cross. According to a report by Prospero di Camulio, another leader in this conflict sang under a tree for the duration of this conflict’s Second Battle of St. Albans. (*) Anne Neville’s successive marriages to combatants on both sides of this conflict corresponded with her father Warwick’s shifting allegiances. This conflict ended with the battle of Bosworth Field, where Henry Tudor defeated Richard III. For 10 points, name this series of 15th century conflicts between York and Lancaster named for a type of flower.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These wars were fought between two cadet branches of the house of Plantagenet. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this lengthy English civil war between the Houses of York and Lancaster, named for the flowers that formed each house's emblem.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Wars of the Roses were largely decided by this 1485 battle in which the forces of Henry Tudor defeated King Richard III.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The House of York was represented by a rose of this color during the Wars of the Roses. Along with blue and red, this color makes up the British flag.

topics.description: A Carthaginian general who invaded Italy by crossing the Alps and was ultimately defeated by Scipio Africanus at the Battle of Zama during the Second Punic War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: During these conflicts, one politician ended every speech by saying that an enemy city “must be destroyed”. That orator, Cato the Elder, traveled to Sicily during the first of these conflicts, accompanying the general Scipio Africanus. During the second of these conflicts, the Battle of (*) Zama saw the defeat of Hannibal Barca. For ten points, name these conflicts which were fought by Rome and Carthage, for control of the Mediterranean.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: During a period of financial stress in this war, the Lex Oppia (op-EE-ah) was passed, limiting women's public display of wealth. The Battle of Ilipa (ill-AH-pa) in this war drove one side out of  Iberia. After being granted emergency dictatorial powers in this war, Quintus Fabius Maximus  adopted a cautious “delaying” strategy. The losing commander of this war was initially victorious  at (*) Trebia, Lake Trasimene (TRAA-sim-een), and Cannae (KAA-nay) after making an arduous crossing  of the Alps. For 10 points, name this war lost by Carthaginian forces under Hannibal.
parts.answer: Second Punic War [prompt on Punic Wars]

topics.description: A country in southeastern Europe, centered on Bucharest and including historic regions such as Moldavia and Transylvania.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An uprising in this country's city of Timișoara (TEE-mee-shwah-rah) eventually led to the toppling of this country's dictator. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Eastern European country which was led by Nicolae Ceaușescu (chow-SHESS-koo) until 1989, when he fled its capital and was executed by firing squad.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Ceaușescu was executed on this holiday. A "truce" named for this holiday occurred when British and German troops abandoned their arms to play soccer on it during World War I.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Ceaușescu banned this practice in Romania, leading to many children being abandoned. This medical procedure was the subject of the Supreme Court case Roe v. Wade.
parts.answer: abortion [do not accept or prompt on "birth control"]

topics.description: The ancient seafaring civilization and peoples of the Levant who developed extensive Mediterranean trade networks, founded or developed cities including Tyre, Byblos, and Carthage, and spread an influential alphabet.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These people developed trade networks around the harvesting of Murex (MOO-reks) rock snails. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these seafaring Mediterranean people who constructed a colony at Carthage and created an  influential alphabet.

parts.label: B
parts.question: High-status Romans wore clothing dyed with Murex products and originally known by a Latin  word that is the origin of this English color term, though many of its ancient shades were closer to red.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This city in modern-day Lebanon was the first capital of the Phoenicians. The Greek pronunciation  of this city's name may be the origin of the term for a certain religious text.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An expensive dye of this color was cultivated from Murex snails. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this color of togas worn by Roman generals celebrating a triumph. This “royal” color was eventually worn exclusively by the Roman Emperor.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The purple dye was alternatively named for this civilization or its city of Tyre. This seafaring civilization from modern-day Lebanon founded cities like Byblos and Carthage.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Phoenicians are credited with developing the first modern one of these systems. The English one of these systems has 26 letters.

topics.description: The 2015 international climate agreement adopted under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to limit global warming.

parts.label: L
parts.question: If successful, this man’s pledge to ban new contracts for oil exploration would make his country the world’s  biggest crude oil exporter to do so. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this left-wing President, who won the 2022 Colombian election while running with the Historic Pact.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Colombia is among the oil producers which have pledged to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius under  this agreement.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Currently, this country is the world’s largest oil producer to stop new exploration. This country’s parliament is  called the Folketing.
parts.answer: Kingdom of Denmark [or Danmarkip Nalagawfia; or Kongarikidh Danmark; or Kongeriget  Danmark]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city’s mayor was elected in 2020 promising to remove on-street parking to help make this city a “15-minute city.” A 2019 public transit strike and the COVID pandemic helped that mayor of this city build bike lanes and ban cars from streets like one named for Rivoli. This city’s mayor, Anne (*) Hidalgo, was also mayor during a 2015 terrorist attack at this city’s Bataclan theater. Another 2015 terrorist attack took place at the offices of the newspaper Charlie Hebdo in this city. Donald Trump withdrew from and Joe Biden rejoined a 2015 international climate agreement signed in this city. For 10 points, name this capital governed from by Emmanuel Macron.
parts.answer: Paris [accept Paris Climate Agreement or Paris Climate Accords]

topics.description: The training and deployment of elephants in warfare, especially in ancient Indian, Hellenistic, and Carthaginian armies.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A treaty involving these animals was negotiated by Megasthenes with Seleucus I, who was paid 500 of them to go away. Pyrrhus of Epirus was the first to try invading Rome using these animals, which were present in most ancient (*) Indian armies. Use of these animals failed at Zama when Scipio Africanus defeated the army of Carthage. For 10 points, name these large animals that Hannibal brought across the Alps.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This figure was among the first rulers of a larger and unified India. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this first great king of India. He came in contact with Seleucus (seh-LOO-siss) I and became a Jain upon his abdication.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Chandragupta was able to conquer much of India by weaponizing these large animals, 500 of which he gifted to Seleucus. These tusked animals were also minted on some Indian coins.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This man was Chandragupta’s grandson. He also receded into a religious life upon his abdication, becoming a Buddhist. This leader ordered several of his proclamations in his Rock Edicts.

topics.description: The Roman emperor of the Julio-Claudian dynasty known for staging major naval spectacles, including one on Lake Fucine.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Naumachiae were events that featured these things. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these things that made up the Classis Misenensis and Classis Ravennas in ancient Rome. The Romans equipped many of these things with a corvus.
parts.answer: Roman ships [accept hexaremes or quinquiremes or quadriremes or triremes or liburnians; accept naves]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Naumachiae were naval battles that were sometimes held in amphitheatres that typically held fights between these people. The retiarius and murmillo were types of these people who fought in the Colosseum.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Before the construction of the Colosseum, this emperor and husband of Agrippina the Younger held a massive naumachia on the Fucine Lake. This emperor’s other maritime spectacles included fighting a killer whale in the harbor of Ostia.
parts.answer: Claudius [or Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus]
